## Publication State

The volume overview pages and their main LaTeX sources are **available** at the reviewed revision. Their notebook companions are **scaffolded**. That means the file and the tutorial title exist. It does not show that the numbers are correct. It does not show that the code runs. It does not show that its dependencies are available. It does not show that results can be reproduced.

The proximal-to-distal monograph is an **available computational publication**. It has a fixed source list. It also has exact PDF, chapter, and evidence contracts. It is not a completed or peer-reviewed textbook. It is not an archival or PID-registered publication. It is not human validation. It is not coaching guidance. It is not a promise about what the software can do.

Use the cards below or the Read menu to move between these pages. The [Article Index](../resources/articles.html) lists the individual chapter pages.

## Core Textbooks and Monographs

::: {.resource-grid .resource-grid--long-form}
::: {.resource-card}
### The Physics of Golf

A textbook on golf. It covers mechanics, control-affine models, multibody dynamics, shaft behavior, impact, and motor control.

[Open The Physics of Golf](../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/index.html){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### The Geometry of Motion

The math behind it all. It covers rigid-body dynamics, nonlinear control, biomechanics, neural control, and simulation.

[Open The Geometry of Motion](../articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/index.html){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Proximal-to-Distal Energy Transfer in the Golf Swing

A technical monograph with 37 chapters. It is fixed to one version. It covers how energy moves through the model. It also covers counterfactual attribution, uncertainty, and falsification. Its results depend on the model. The limits of the evidence remain open.

[Open the Technical Monograph](../articles/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/index.html){.resource-link}
[Download the Exact 252-Page PDF](../articles/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/proximal_distal_energy_transfer.pdf){.resource-link}
:::
:::

## Proximal-to-Distal Study Library

Use the technical monograph as the main reference. It is fixed to one version. Choose the companion for an easier read. Choose the summary for a shorter overview. Choose the workbench to try model runs. A model result holds only for its declared system, state, inputs, and comparison. None of these routes shows human validation. None shows a swing that works for everyone.

- [Technical Monograph](../articles/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/index.html): the computational publication, with its exact sources, equations, claims, falsifiers, and evidence ledgers.
- [How a Golf Swing Carries Energy](../articles/proximal-distal-a-journey-through-the-swing.html): a 30-chapter visual companion with the same limits on how to read it.
- [Technical Summary](../articles/proximal-distal-energy-transfer.html): a shorter route through the main counterfactual and energy arguments.
- [Interactive Model Workbench](../articles/proximal-distal-model-workbench.html): guided experiments to explore. Their outputs are not measured golfer data.

## Book Series Volumes

::: {.resource-grid}
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume 0: The Mathematical Primer

The math basics. They cover linear algebra, state space, Lie groups, screw theory, and recursive kinematics.

[Open Volume 0 Main Page](../articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/volume0.html){.resource-link}
[Start with Chapter 1](../articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/vol0_ch01_linear_algebra.html){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume I: Tangent-Space Methods for Nonlinear Control

How small changes grow. It covers exact first-variation equations and the limits for finite changes. It also covers contraction, local optimal control, and counterfactual splits that depend on the model.

[Open Volume I Main Page](tangent-space-methods.html){.resource-link}
[Start with Chapter 1](tangent-space-methods.html#book1-ch1){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume II: Control Is Motion

Control built around trajectories. It also gives the geometric mechanics view of high-dimensional motion.

[Open Volume II Main Page](control-is-motion.html){.resource-link}
[Review source, scaffolded notebook, and chapter states](control-is-motion.html#book2-ch1){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume III: Biomechanics - Biology to Systems

From rigid bodies to biology. It covers biological models and experiment pipelines. It also covers inference workflows.

[Open Volume III Main Page](biomechanics-biology-to-systems.html){.resource-link}
[Review source, scaffolded notebook, and chapter states](biomechanics-biology-to-systems.html#book3-ch1){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume IV: Human Motor Control

How people control movement. It covers neural structure and dimensionality reduction. It also covers internal models and movement intelligence for engineered systems.

[Open Volume IV Main Page](human-motor-control.html){.resource-link}
[Review source, scaffolded notebook, and chapter states](human-motor-control.html#book4-ch1){.resource-link}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### Volume V: Practical Application

Putting it into practice. It covers a companion computing platform. It also covers software verification and practical integration.

[View Volume V PDF](../articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/Volume_V/main.pdf){.resource-link}
[Review LaTeX Source](https://github.com/D-sorganization/AffineDrift/blob/main/articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/Volume_V/main.tex){.resource-link}
:::
:::
